pr_title: Add resolution to Amcrest camera unique id
pr_body:
## Proposed change

The current unique id assigned to the Amcrest camera is based on the device serial number. However, the camera supports multiple streams which have different resolutions. Add this information to the unique id to allow each stream to be configured as a separate camera.

pr_comments: I tweaked this a bit so it will only change the unique id if the camera is explicitly set to low resolution. This should hopefully limit the blast radius of the breaking change.

“ This may leave orphaned camera entities with the old unique id that would need to be manually deleted” is a sentence I really try to avoid.

You know in the code when there is a config entry with an old unique so at least delete it, so the user do not have to search (and once deleted it is pretty easy to recreate with the new id).
You should do it in async_setup_platform, there might be other places, but this one is secure.

I added some migration logic that will look for the entity with the old unique id and if it exists then update it with the new unique id. Let me know if you think this is what you were thinking. I tested this by launching an HA instance with the camera configured on the current `dev` branch (which creates the entity with the previous unique id), then change to this branch and launch HA again. I see the update message fire and the camera entity persists through the update.
@janiversen @ludeeus Anything else that is needed here? It would be great to get this bugfix in before 2021.10 betas start to get cut!
for me its OK, but I would like to hear the opinion og @ludeeus
Rebased the PR onto the latest `dev` to deal with the CI issue.

issue_context.title: Arcmcrest component
issue_context.body:
### The problem

Im using core-2021.8.7
After upgrade to core-2021.9.6 a noticed problem in using my Dahua cameras.

I had defined two cams from one device, because in some dashboards i need low quality, on other dasboards i need full hq. My config is like this:

amcrest:
  - host: 192.168.1.100
    username: admin
    password: password
    name: Cam1 LQ
    resolution: low
  - host: 192.168.1.100
    username: admin
    password: password
    resolution: high
    name: Cam1

After upgrade Home Assistant generating id for this two entities from his names like : 'Cam1 LQ' -> camera.cam1_lq
in is error that armcres not generating unique id and xxxxxxxxxxxxxx alredy exists. I see only firmst entity. Its not possible to define two entity from one device. Maybe add possibility to define unique_id:

Not I downgraded HA to core-2021.8.7

### What is version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2021.9.6

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

core-2021.8.7 - checked and working well

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

armcrest

comments:
Hey there @flacjacket, mind taking a look at this issue as it has been labeled with an integration (`amcrest`) you are listed as a [code owner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L41) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

This is an interesting problem. I am wondering if it would be possible to change how the camera is configured to allow both of the camera configurations to be derived from the same device. I guess regardless we would need to set some extra values in the unique id of the cameras.
The one thing I am worried about is the other parameters being used, such as stream source or ffmpeg arguments, and just needing to keep adding additional values to the unique id.
Maybe good option is add definition _resolution: both_ and with this option create automatically two camera entities?
#56207 provides a fix for this by disambiguating the cameras by the resolution. By providing both through a single configuration makes naming each of the cameras more difficult, IMO.

review_comments: For the Logger, we should use lazy formating and not assign a local constants with templates if we can
I'm not sure what is the policy for deprecating this migration logic.

The only policy is to let it stay for a long time, because many do not upgrade every month. I just removed similar code in tradfri after 2 years.  In other words leave it until you have a good reason to remove it.
I think the `type: ignore` is needed here because of the lambda. Any thoughts on how to get mypy to know what this is would be appreciated.
I still have not seen a good solution, and according to google this is a major deficit.
The value is striped everywhere else, why is that not needed here?
Good catch, thanks. Added the `.strip()` for the serial number.
